title: Deep-PPG – Study on the suitability of VCSEL and LED for recording vital parameters
summary:
The goal of the study is to improve the robustness and signal quality of wearables. The PPG curve is recorded here through a non-invasive optical measurement. A light-emitting diode (LED) and a photodetector on the surface of the skin measure the photoplethysmographic (PPG) signal. The PPG signal is generated by the volumetric changes in blood circulation due to the heartbeat. The crucial electronic components (LED and photodiode) for recording a simple PPG signal are cost-effective and compact. This, combined with low power requirements, makes the method ideal for integration into compact mobile systems.
However, the robustness of the measurement against motion artifacts is far from adequate. Particularly in the stress range during physical activities, the susceptibility of the PPG signal to the wearer's movement becomes apparent. The causes of disturbances are movements of the sensor over the tissue, tissue compression due to changes in pressing force, and changes in blood flow dynamics.
The study is conducted to evaluate the use of Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers (VCSEL) as a light source for recording vital parameters. VCSELs have higher selectivity compared to LEDs due to their beam profile, which is directed (about 18-25°). Conventional LEDs emit light in a Lambertian pattern. The photoplethysmographic (PPG) curve of the subjects is measured using wearables with LEDs and VCSELs and compared. The data obtained will be used to evaluate whether VCSELs are suitable as emitters for the acquisition of vital parameters instead of LEDs. So far, there have been no studies on VCSELs as emitters in wearables.
conditions: No statements are made about the physiological condition of the study population.

interventions.name:
Observational study.
The study investigates the signal quality of PPG measurements in wearables, comparing Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers (VCSEL) with conventional LEDs. PPG data will be simultaneously recorded using both light sources to evaluate the robustness and quality of the signals,

BMI < 30

Known previous illnesses (physical/mental)
BMI >= 30
